title: Pressure Under Water
description: Baron Standstill floods a chamber to trap shard 5. To dive safely, learn how liquids press in every direction — and harder the deeper you go.

content.value: Liquids have weight, so they exert pressure on the bottom AND the walls of their container. Unlike a solid, a liquid presses in ALL directions — sideways, downward, and even upward.

The deeper you go in a liquid, the more liquid sits above you pressing down — so the pressure INCREASES with depth. That is why a dam is built much thicker at the bottom than at the top: the water pressure is greatest deep down.

Water tank with holes at different heights:

│●→        (top hole: low pressure, weak squirt)
│ ●→→
│  ●→→→    (bottom hole: high pressure, strong squirt)
└────────
Deeper hole = higher pressure = water shoots out farther.

At the same depth, the pressure of a liquid is the same in every direction. Pressure does not depend on the shape of the container — only on the depth (and the liquid itself). A heavier (denser) liquid presses harder at the same depth.
Deep-sea divers wear strong suits because water pressure deep in the ocean is enormous — hundreds of times greater than at the surface.

Key Takeaway: Liquids exert pressure in all directions, and the pressure increases with depth. At a given depth the pressure is the same in every direction, which is why dams are thicker at the bottom.

quiz.question: As you go deeper in water, the pressure…
quiz.explain: More liquid sits above you at greater depth, so the pressure increases with depth.

quiz.question: A liquid exerts pressure…
quiz.explain: Liquids press downward, sideways and upward — in all directions.

quiz.question: Why is a dam built thicker at its base than at the top?
options: To save material at the top
Because water pressure is greatest at the bottom
quiz.explain: Water pressure increases with depth, so the base must be strong enough to withstand the greatest pressure.
